aions_core/aions_hybrid_retrieval.py: A search system that combines three different ways of finding information—keyword matching using BM25 scoring, vector similarity search, and intelligent reranking with machine learning models—to give better search results than any single method alone. It loads knowledge from an existing AIONS system and other sources, processes search queries by running them through all three methods, then merges and ranks the results to show the most relevant information first. The system tracks statistics on how often each search method is used and how fast searches happen. It takes search queries as input and returns ranked lists of relevant documents with scores and metadata about which method found each result. It integrates with the original AIONS knowledge base, vector search databases, and optionally uses cross-encoder models to rerank results for better quality.
aions_core/aions_reformed_integration.py: A question-answering system that loads factual information from organized seed data files covering topics like capitals, math, science, programming, and history, and combines it with a memory management system to answer user questions. It implements a step-by-step process: first checking for direct matches in seed data, then looking up more complex knowledge, and finally falling back to a memory system for unknown topics. The system handles aliases by replacing one word with another, applies patches for known incorrect answers, and supports Polish language queries. Input is a user question, output is a structured response with the answer, confidence score, and the source layer where the answer came from. It integrates with seed data files organized by topic and a memory system for handling questions the basic data doesn't cover.
aions_core/ingest_cbms_data.py: A data loading tool that reads JSON files from a specific folder and uploads them into a vector database (LanceDB) so they can be searched by similarity matching. It processes chunks of text one at a time in batches of 100, converts each text into a numerical representation using a machine learning model, and stores these embeddings in the database alongside the original text and file paths. The tool tracks progress with a progress bar and measures how fast the loading is happening. Input is JSON files containing text content, output is vectors stored in LanceDB with associated metadata. It communicates with the sentence-transformers library to generate embeddings and writes the results into a vector table.
aions_core/server/cbms_memory.py: An artificial intelligence memory system that chunks up and organizes knowledge into small pieces so an AI can recall relevant information quickly when answering questions. It saves knowledge chunks to disk with unique IDs, builds indexes using Korean-style syllable matching and optional symbolic codes for faster lookups, and has safeguards to prevent saving garbage or repetitive responses that aren't real knowledge. The system tracks what knowledge exists, generates thinking traces showing how it retrieved and synthesized information, and allows learning new things through a decision gate that rejects noise and echo. Input is knowledge to learn and questions to answer, output is retrieved information and synthesized responses. It stores chunks as JSON files and maintains a manifest of all knowledge with timestamps and access counts.
aions_core/server/cbms_symbolic_index.py: A lookup table that converts written text into symbolic codes so questions can be matched against stored knowledge using those codes instead of raw words. It builds itself by reading all stored knowledge chunks, converting each one's text into Esperanto (an international language), then encoding that into CBMS codes (compact symbolic representations). When you search, the tool converts your question to the same Esperanto-based codes, then looks up which knowledge chunks use those same codes, ranking them by how many codes matched. Input is knowledge chunks and a search query, output is ranked chunks sorted by match strength. It uses an Esperanto bridge library to handle language conversion and a codebook engine to manage the symbolic encoding system.
aions_core/server/web_rag_cbms.py: A web-scraping integration that fetches current facts from the internet when the AI system doesn't have an answer stored locally, then injects those facts into memory as temporary knowledge chunks. It searches Wikipedia, Stack Overflow, GitHub, and documentation sites for information related to the user's question, extracts relevant sentences, scores them by how well they match the query, and converts them to memory chunks with source citations. The system is respectful to websites by pausing between requests and only trusts certain safe domains. Input is a user query that triggered a 'don't know' response, output is temporary memory chunks with citations to source URLs and relevance scores. It communicates with websites over HTTPS, parses HTML to extract clean text, and registers facts as temporary chunks in the memory system.
aions_core/tools/check_status.py: A diagnostic tool that connects to a local status endpoint and prints out any errors that have been recorded. It makes an HTTP request to a server running on the same machine, asks for statistics, and displays the error list in JSON format. Input is nothing (the tool uses hardcoded defaults), output is a printed list of errors. It communicates with an HTTP server listening on port 8080 of the local machine at the status path.
control_plane/blends/search_blends.py: A command-line tool for searching through a library of documented solutions and lessons learned from past problems and their analyses. It takes a search query with keywords about a topic or problem, looks it up against stored blend records which combine observed mistakes with their analyses and conclusions, and returns the best matching lessons learned with confidence scores. Each result shows the blend ID, domain, and the key rule or insight. The search works offline without needing the internet. Input is search keywords and optional result limit parameter, output is formatted search results as plain text or JSON showing matching lessons and their confidence scores.
control_plane/skills/schema.py: A data definition file that describes what an AIONS object looks like and what fields are required for different types of things the system can do. It defines a single unified model (AObject) that represents any skill, recipe, workflow, knowledge item, or decision rule with fields for identification, type, description, requirements, handlers that execute them, and risk level. It validates that each object has the right fields for its type—for example, executable skills need a handler function, and recipes need steps. Input is a path to a JSON file or structured data to load, output is an AObject instance or a list of validation errors. The file is purely structural; it defines the schema and provides functions for loading and validating objects.
mcpServers/VS_CODE_MCP_CODEX/src/__main_: An entry point that starts an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server allowing remote clients to connect and use AIONS as a code analysis tool. It checks that the Python environment is inside a virtual environment to prevent accidental system-wide installation, handles Windows-specific fixes for standard input and output, and launches the server in one of three network modes: direct pipe communication for local use, HTTP for optional remote LAN access, or special event-stream protocol. The server accepts environment variables to configure networking options and security settings. Input is command-line arguments and environment variables, output is a running MCP server accepting JSON-RPC protocol requests. It coordinates with the actual server implementation and handles cross-platform network setup.
scripts/aions_node_heartbeat.py: A monitoring agent that periodically sends health-check signals to a central coordinator service so it knows this machine is still running and working properly. It sends POST requests to a core API every 60 seconds by default, reports the node's health status and current CPU load percentage, and logs any network failures to standard error. It can read the node ID from configuration files or environment variables, allowing it to identify itself to the coordinator. Input is configuration such as node name, API address, and check interval, output is log messages and periodic network requests to the core API. It communicates with the AIONS core API over HTTP using JSON-formatted POST requests.
scripts/full_system_scan.py: An orchestrator that inventories all files across all hard drives, analyzes code dependencies and project structure, and generates a master report showing which projects exist on the system. It runs in three phases: first it gets a complete file list per drive using the Everything search tool, then it runs detailed code analysis per drive to find dependencies and duplicates, and finally it detects project roots by looking for markers like .git or package.json files. Input is optional drive letters to scan in order (defaults to all except special backing volumes), output is CSV inventories, detailed scan reports, and a master map JSON file with all discovered projects and their locations. It uses the Everything desktop search tool to enumerate files and runs subprocess commands for the turbo scanner analysis.
scripts/set_aions_cache_env.sh: A configuration script that sets up directory locations for temporary files and downloaded packages, redirecting them from system defaults to a specific development folder on the D drive to keep the system drive clean. It configures environment variables for pip package cache, Python temporary files, Hugging Face machine learning model downloads, PyTorch library cache, Docker configuration, and other development tool caches, all pointing to centralized paths under a single AIONS cache root. This approach organizes all development caches in one place and prevents clutter on the system drive. Input is nothing or the AIONS_CACHE_ROOT environment variable override, output is set environment variables and created directories ready for use by development tools.
scripts/smoke_http_mcp.py: A quick test that verifies an AIONS MCP server is running and responding correctly over HTTP protocol. It sends a standard initialization handshake to the server asking it to identify itself and list available tools, reads the response, and checks if both the handshake and tool listing succeeded. It demonstrates that the server is alive and the network protocol works properly. Input is optional URL parameter defaulting to local port 8787, output is printed status messages showing server name and tool count plus exit code 0 for success or 1 for failure. It communicates with an HTTP endpoint using JSON-RPC protocol with server-sent events, making raw HTTP requests.
server/context_schema.py: A data structure that stores metadata about conversation turns and messages—information about when something happened, who said it, what role they had, what they were doing, and when the information expires. It normalizes messy metadata into a clean, consistent format with fields for agent name, speaker role, source system, turn number, tags, timestamps, and time-to-live expiration days. It handles various input formats like timestamps as strings or date objects, tags as lists or individual strings, and converts them all to standard representations. Input is raw metadata dictionaries or dataclass objects, output is normalized, serializable dictionaries with proper types and expiration calculations. The module is purely for defining and converting metadata structures rather than doing runtime work.
